question.prompt:
The base of the pentahedron shown below is a \(13 \times 8\) rectangle, and its lateral faces are two isosceles triangles with base of length \(8\) and congruent sides of length \(13,\) and two isosceles trapezoids with bases of lengths \(7\) and \(13\) and nonparallel sides of length \(13.\)

[Figure 1](figures/2025_AMC_12A_Q20_question_fig1.svg)

What is the volume of the pentahedron?

solutions.explanation:
The length-7 top edge suggests separating the solid into a middle portion and two ends. First we need the perpendicular height.

The top edge is parallel to the length-13 sides of the rectangular base because these edges are the parallel bases of the trapezoids. In an isosceles trapezoid the shorter base is centered along the longer one: dropping perpendiculars creates two right triangles with equal hypotenuses and equal heights, so their end offsets are equal. Each offset here is
\[
\frac{13-7}{2}=3.
\]
The equal sides of each triangular face also place its apex halfway across the width \(8\). Thus the horizontal projection of a sloping edge of length \(13\) runs \(3\) units along the rectangle and \(4\) units across it. If \(h>0\) is the solid's perpendicular height, two applications of the Pythagorean theorem give
\[
h^2+3^2+4^2=13^2,
\qquad h=\sqrt{144}=12.
\]
Cut by planes perpendicular to the length-13 direction through the two endpoints of the top edge. The middle piece is a triangular prism of length \(7\). Its triangular cross-section has base \(8\) and perpendicular height \(12\), so its volume is
\[
V_{\text{middle}}=7\left(\frac12\cdot8\cdot12\right)=336.
\]
Each end piece is a pyramid whose base is a \(3\times8\) rectangle in the original base plane. Its apex is the corresponding top-edge endpoint, at perpendicular height \(12\). Each therefore has volume
\[
V_{\text{end}}=\frac13(3\cdot8)(12)=96.
\]
These three pieces fill the solid and share only boundary faces. The total volume is
\[
V=336+2(96)=\boxed{528},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
solutions.title: A prism and two pyramids

solutions.explanation:
We can complete the solid to a triangular prism and subtract the two pieces added at its ends.

First determine the ridge's position and height. The parallel bases of the isosceles trapezoids make the top edge parallel to the length-13 direction. Their equal legs give equal end offsets, since the perpendicular end triangles have the same height and equal hypotenuses. Thus the top edge is inset
\[
\frac{13-7}{2}=3
\]
from each end. The isosceles triangular faces place the ridge halfway across the width, \(4\) units from either long side. Consequently, a sloping edge of length \(13\) has horizontal components \(3\) and \(4\). The perpendicular height \(h>0\) satisfies
\[
h^2=13^2-3^2-4^2=144,
\qquad h=12.
\]
Extend the ridge at the same height to lie directly above the midpoints of both length-8 base edges. Filling out to these extended endpoints produces a triangular prism of length \(13\). Its triangular end faces have area
\[
K=\frac12\cdot8\cdot12=48.
\]
At each end, the added piece is a tetrahedron. Its base is the prism's triangular end face, and its opposite vertex is the original ridge endpoint. The perpendicular distance from that vertex to the end-face plane is the horizontal inset \(3\). Each added tetrahedron therefore has volume
\[
\frac13\cdot48\cdot3=48.
\]
The two added pieces occupy opposite ends and do not overlap. Removing them from the completed prism gives
\[
V=13\cdot48-2(48)=\boxed{528},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
solutions.title: Complete a triangular prism
